thread.title: JPMorgan Chase using tax cut to boost wages, add jobs and increase lending

author: Mike Sunnucks
title: JPMorgan Chase using tax cut to boost wages, add jobs and increase lending
text: – Senior Reporter, Phoenix   12:52pm EST JPMorgan Chase & Co. is giving employees raises and bonuses as part of a $20 billion, five-year U.S. investment effort in the wake of the tax cuts passed by Congress. JPMorgan (NYSE: JPM) joins a chorus of other big and regional banks and other companies giving bonuses, raises and increasing investments. Chase said it will raise workers' pay from between $12 and $16.50 per hour to $15 and $18 per hour. In more expensive markets such as New York, New Jersey and San Francisco, workers will see base pay increase to $18 per hour. Workers in Chicago and Detroit will get raises to $16.50. The raises will benefit 22,000 Chase employees working at branches and customer service employees. Chase employees will also be getting a $750 bonus and Chase is cutting health insurance costs $750 per year for employees making less than $60,000. JPMorgan also plans on hiring 4,000 new workers, opening new branches and increasing small business lending by $4 billion. JPMorgan Chase is one of Central Ohio's largest employers , with about 18,600 area workers, according to Columbus Business First research. Chase joins Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC) and a number of other banks in offering bonuses or raises to employees after the tax cuts were passed last month. “Over 99 percent of American companies are small to mid-sized businesses and account for over half of the jobs created in the U.S. This important segment of the economy drives growth and is critical to the health of our communities” Doug Petno , CEO of JPMorgan Commercial Banking, said in a press release. Chase’s $20 billion plan comes after Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) announced a $350 billion, five-year U.S. investment boost stemming from the tax cuts. – Senior Reporter, Phoenix   12:52pm EST
